manualReview: SPANISH SOURCE, SPANISH REBUILD. document.language is 'es' and every block is verbatim from the OHCHR Spanish rendering; this is the original-language rebuild, not a translation (variant: original).
ARTICLE 2 IS TWO PARAGRAPHS. Unlike the English rendering, the Spanish source sets Artículo 2 as two separate paragraphs ('Toda persona...' and 'Además...'); both were kept as separate blocks.
SENTENCES REJOINED ACROSS PAGES. The Artículo 10 paragraph spans printed pages 3-4 and was rejoined into one block assigned to page 3.

LISTS SPLIT ACROSS PAGES. Artículo 14's two clauses straddle pages 4-5 (item 1 on page 4, item 2 on page 5); the list is assigned to page 4. Artículo 29's heading falls at the bottom of page 8 with its clauses on page 9; the list is assigned to page 9.
NUMBERED CLAUSES AS ORDERED LISTS. Articles 11, 13-17, 20, 21, 23, 25-27, and 29 use the source's own clause numbering, rendered as ordered lists; single-clause articles remain paragraphs.

ATTRIBUTION LINE KEPT. The Spanish rendering includes an adoption line ('Adoptada y proclamada por la Asamblea General...') absent from the English rendering; it is kept as a paragraph under the title.
NO PAGE FURNITURE, NO IMAGES. The source pages carry no running heads, footers, page numbers, or figures.
BORN-DIGITAL SOURCE. The PDF has a text layer, so source_token_recall in the accessibility report independently measures this plan; transcription was performed by reading.
LICENSE. Public-domain UN document; OHCHR PDF rendering used for local accessibility testing.
Compare every page of the rebuild with the source; automated checks cannot verify meaning.
